newsitem.title: UK: LCE coffee ends switch-backed ride softer - SEPT 11.
newsitem.headline: LCE coffee ends switch-backed ride softer - SEPT 11.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended a choppy session weaker on Wednesday after a slide in New York arabica futures sparked losses in London, traders said.
"It is all about New York," said one trader.

New York coffee prices on Wednesday slumped to their lowest level in one month after the CSCE announced its intention to slash to 200 from 500 lots the speculative position limit on contracts in the notice period.
The recommendation is to be voted on by the board at its meeting later on Wednesday.
But London traders said the move would do little to affect the market since most big speculators usually have closed out their positions by the notice period.
"Most of the speculators are out before the notice period," said one.
He did add, however, that if approved the move would make it extremely difficult for any speculator to squeeze the New York market.
At the close on Wednesday the benchmark November contract was off $7 at $1,545 a tonne and well off a session high of $1,566 a tonne.
The spot September contract was down $13 at $1,595 a tonne after touching a high of $1,623 a tonne.
September's premium to November had narrowed to $50 a tonne by the close on Wednesday as gradings increased, said traders.
Turnover on the exchange reached 3,873 lots on Wednesday.
Traders on Wednesday noted good roaster buying and bargain hunting as prices slid.
